claims.title: Shopper order data may be readable across the public-to-storefront boundary
claims.description: `flow:entity:shopper>process:storefront-api>place-order` crosses from `boundary:public-internet` to `process:storefront-api` and carries order contents, shipping addresses, and card last-four data, but `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If that attribute resolves to no effective transport encryption, an attacker able to observe this public-facing path can intercept shoppers' order and identity data in transit. The disclosed shopper and order details can subsequently be used to target accounts or correlate records later stored in `store:orders-db`; this draft is conditional on the unverified transport control.

quotes.text: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through the storefront API
Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on `unknown:flow:entity:shopper>process:storefront-api>place-order:encryption_in_transit`: the flow crosses the public-internet boundary, so an observer can plausibly target it, but must obtain an on-path position. Impact is high because the order path carries PII and financial details, including shopper addresses and card last-four data.

mitigations.summary: Verify and require TLS for shopper order submission
mitigations.detail: Set and enforce TLS 1.2+ for `flow:entity:shopper>process:storefront-api>place-order`, including certificate validation at the shopper-facing endpoint.

mitigations.summary: Reduce payment-related fields in the order request
mitigations.detail: Avoid carrying payment-adjacent fields unless necessary and use opaque payment references where the order service can resolve them.

claims.title: Settlement confirmations may be readable on the processor webhook path
claims.description: `flow:entity:card-processor>process:storefront-api>settlement-webhook` crosses from the public internet to `process:storefront-api`, while both its protocol and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If the webhook transport is not effectively encrypted, an on-path attacker can intercept settlement confirmations and learn payment-status information for orders. That information can be correlated with order records processed by `process:storefront-api` and `process:order-service`, enabling targeted fraud or customer reconnaissance; this is conditional on the unresolved transport posture.

quotes.text: After they settle a payment they POST a webhook back to the storefront API to tell us the order is paid.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on `unknown:flow:entity:card-processor>process:storefront-api>settlement-webhook:encryption_in_transit`: the webhook crosses the public-internet boundary, but interception still requires an on-path position. Impact is medium because the exposed settlement status is financial information about an order, although the modeled callback carries a settlement confirmation rather than the full order record.

mitigations.summary: Require HTTPS/TLS for the processor webhook
mitigations.detail: Document and enforce TLS 1.2+ with certificate validation for `flow:entity:card-processor>process:storefront-api>settlement-webhook`.
Carry only an opaque settlement reference and resolve any additional payment details inside the protected order-processing path.

claims.title: Order and address data may be readable between the storefront and order service
claims.description: `flow:process:storefront-api>process:order-service>submit-order` crosses from `boundary:storefront-dmz` to `boundary:core-services` and carries order contents, shopper identifiers, and shipping addresses, but its `encryption_in_transit` value is unknown. If transport protection is absent or ineffective, an attacker who gains an observation point on that cross-zone path can intercept PII and financial order information. The captured identifiers and order details can be correlated with the confidential records subsequently read and written through `flow:process:order-service>store:orders-db>read-write-orders`; this draft does not assert that the gRPC link is plaintext.

quotes.text: When a shopper submits an order the storefront API calls the order service over gRPC.
Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on `unknown:flow:process:storefront-api>process:order-service>submit-order:encryption_in_transit`: observing the DMZ-to-core crossing requires a network foothold, but no verified transport control is stated. Impact is high because the flow carries shopper identifiers, addresses, and financial order data toward the confidential orders dataset.

mitigations.summary: Use mTLS on the storefront-to-order-service call
mitigations.detail: Require TLS 1.2+ with mutual service authentication for `flow:process:storefront-api>process:order-service>submit-order`.

mitigations.summary: Minimize sensitive fields carried across zones
mitigations.detail: Pass opaque order references where possible and have `process:order-service` retrieve only the needed data through protected internal access.

claims.title: Order database traffic may expose the confidential order corpus in transit
claims.description: `flow:process:order-service>store:orders-db>read-write-orders` carries order rows, shipping addresses, and card last-four data to `store:orders-db`, but its protocol and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If this database connection lacks effective encryption, an attacker with a foothold on the core-services path can intercept database reads or writes and obtain confidential PII and financial order data. Captured records provide the same information the order service uses to produce completed-order receipts in `store:receipt-archive`; this is conditional on the unverified transport configuration.

quotes.text: Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database (orders-db) that the order service reads and writes

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional on `unknown:flow:process:order-service>store:orders-db>read-write-orders:encryption_in_transit`: the attacker needs a foothold on an internal core-services path, although no verified transport protection is stated. Impact is high because `store:orders-db` is confidential and holds shopper addresses and card-last-four data.

mitigations.detail: Require TLS for `flow:process:order-service>store:orders-db>read-write-orders`, validate the database certificate, and prefer mutual authentication where supported.
Allow database connections only from `process:order-service` and monitor unexpected connections or packet-capture-capable hosts in the core-services environment.

claims.title: A copied orders database may disclose shopper and payment data if storage encryption is absent
claims.description: `store:orders-db` is classified confidential and holds PII and financial data, while `encryption_at_rest` is unknown. If the store and its operational copies are not encrypted at rest, an attacker who obtains a database volume, snapshot, backup, or decommissioned copy can read orders, shopper addresses, and card last-four data without using the normal order-service access path. The disclosure supplies a corpus of customer and payment-adjacent information that can be correlated with settlement and receipt records; this is explicitly conditional on the unresolved at-rest encryption attribute.

quotes.text: Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database (orders-db)

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on `unknown:store:orders-db:encryption_at_rest`: obtaining a storage-layer copy requires access to an operational artifact, but the model provides no verified at-rest protection. Impact is high because the store is confidential and contains PII and financial data for the order corpus.

mitigations.summary: Establish and enforce encryption at rest for orders data
mitigations.detail: Verify the setting for `store:orders-db`, then require managed-key or customer-managed-key encryption for the primary database and every backup, snapshot, replica, and decommissioned copy.
Restrict export, snapshot, backup, and key-use permissions to dedicated operational roles and audit all copy and restore operations.

claims.title: Recovering the order-service database password enables bulk reading of orders
claims.description: The application-account password used on `flow:process:order-service>store:orders-db>read-write-orders` is kept in an environment variable on `process:order-service`, and that account has full read/write access to `store:orders-db`. An attacker who compromises the worker or its runtime can recover that credential and use the account's existing grant to read the confidential order corpus, including shopper addresses and card-last-four data. Second-order, the recovered database access bypasses per-request storefront sessions and exposes records at corpus scale rather than only the order associated with one shopper request.

quotes.text: The password comes from an environment variable on the worker.
a single application account that has full read/write

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because recovery requires control of `process:order-service` or its runtime, but the credential is explicitly held in that worker's environment. Impact is high because `assertion:authorization-grant~principal:application-account~s.96924e46de53~v.527ec0f9b94c` states full read/write access to confidential `store:orders-db`, which holds PII and financial order data.

mitigations.detail: Use workload identity or short-lived database credentials issued from a dedicated secret manager rather than retaining the application-account password in the worker environment.

mitigations.summary: Reduce the application account's read scope
mitigations.detail: Split duties into narrowly scoped database principals and grant `process:order-service` only the rows, columns, and operations necessary for its order-processing role.
Rotate the existing application-account password, audit credential retrieval, and alert on query volumes or sources inconsistent with `process:order-service`.
